title: Can You Extend Your Visa, and How?
excerpt: Visa extension guide: when you can extend a visit visa, Schengen, UK, US and other rules, documents, timing, fees, what happens while you wait, and 8 easy steps to apply.
content:
Short answer: A visa extension lets you stay longer in a country than your current visa or permission allows, but only if that country's rules permit it and you apply before your current permission ends. Some countries allow visitors to extend easily at an immigration office, others allow it only in exceptional situations such as illness or a cancelled flight, and some do not allow visitors to extend at all. Always apply before your stay expires, keep proof of your application, and never assume you can stay while you wait unless the rules say so.

Quick factsDetails
When to applyBefore your current permission ends
WhereUsually the immigration office or online system of the country you are in
Common reasonsIllness, cancelled flights, family emergencies, extra tourism where allowed
Visit visasSome countries allow it, others only in exceptional cases
OverstayingCan lead to fines, removal and bans

Table of Contents

  • What is a visa extension?
  • When can you get a visa extension?
  • How does a Schengen visa extension work?
  • Can you extend a UK visitor visa?
  • Can you extend a US visitor visa?
  • Other countries: a quick overview
  • What are the 8 easy steps to apply for a visa extension?
  • Which documents do you usually need?
  • Can you stay while you wait for a decision?
  • What happens if your visa extension is refused?
  • How do you write a request letter for a visa extension?
  • Visa extension or a new visa: which is better?
  • What if you have a medical emergency?
  • How much does it cost?
  • A real example: a cancelled flight in Spain
  • Which visa extension mistakes should you avoid?
  • Key takeaways
  • How can Alif Visa help with a visa extension?
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Sources

What is a visa extension?

A visa extension is official permission to stay longer than the date on your current visa or entry stamp. It is granted by the immigration authority of the country you are in, not by the embassy that issued your visa. Depending on the country, it may be added to your passport as a new sticker, stamp or electronic record.

A visa extension is different from a new visa. A new visa usually means leaving the country and applying again, while an extension keeps you in the country legally under your current status for longer.

When can you get a visa extension?

The rules vary widely, but most countries fall into one of three groups:

  1. Extension allowed for visitors. Some countries let tourists apply for a visa extension at an immigration office for a fee, often for a set number of extra days.
  2. Extension only in exceptional cases. Others, including Schengen countries, allow it only for reasons such as serious illness, force majeure or important personal reasons.
  3. No extension for visitors. Some countries expect visitors to leave and apply again from home if they want to stay longer, and only allow extensions in very limited situations.

How does a Schengen visa extension work?

Under the EU Visa Code, a Schengen visa can be extended in a few situations:

  • Force majeure, such as a cancelled flight, natural disaster or sudden closure of borders
  • Humanitarian reasons, such as serious illness or an accident
  • Serious personal reasons, such as the illness or death of a close relative
  • Late entry, in some cases where you entered later than planned and have not used all your days

You apply to the immigration authorities in the country where you are, before your visa ends. You will usually need your passport, proof of the reason (for example a medical certificate), proof of funds and insurance that covers the extra days. The total stay must still respect the 90/180 rule in most cases. Our Schengen calculator guide explains how to count your days.

Can you extend a UK visitor visa?

Visitors to the UK can normally stay up to six months. A visa extension beyond that is usually only possible in limited cases, such as private medical treatment, certain academic visitors or exceptional circumstances. Most visitors who want to come back for longer should leave and apply again for the correct visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules for your situation.

Can you extend a US visitor visa?

In the United States, the length of stay is set by your admission record (I-94), not the visa itself. Many B1/B2 visitors can apply to extend their stay by filing Form I-539 with US Citizenship and Immigration Services before the I-94 date expires. You must show a genuine reason, enough funds and that you will leave at the end. Some visitors, such as those who entered under the Visa Waiver Program with an ESTA, generally cannot extend.

Other countries: a quick overview

CountryGeneral approach for visitors
Schengen countriesOnly for force majeure, humanitarian or serious personal reasons
United KingdomLimited cases; most visitors leave and reapply
United StatesForm I-539 for many B visa holders; not for ESTA visitors
ThailandTourists can often apply at an immigration office for extra days
United Arab EmiratesSome tourist visas can be extended through official channels
TurkeyShort-term residence permits for longer stays, applied for in-country

These are general patterns, and rules change. Always check the official immigration website of the country you are in.

What are the 8 easy steps to apply for a visa extension?

  1. Check the rules for your visa type on the official immigration website.
  2. Count your days and note the exact end date of your current permission.
  3. Gather evidence for your reason: medical certificate, cancelled flight notice or family letter.
  4. Show funds for the extra time, such as recent bank statements.
  5. Extend your insurance to cover the new dates.
  6. Book a return ticket or show onward travel for after the new end date.
  7. Apply before your stay ends, online or at the immigration office, and pay the fee.
  8. Keep proof of your application and follow any instructions about waiting for a decision.

Which documents do you usually need?

  • Passport valid for the extra period
  • Current visa or entry stamp
  • Application form for the visa extension
  • Passport photos, if required
  • Evidence of the reason for staying longer
  • Proof of funds
  • Proof of accommodation for the extra days
  • Travel insurance covering the new dates
  • Return or onward ticket
  • Fee payment

Can you stay while you wait for a decision?

This depends on the country. In some places, applying before your stay ends allows you to remain while your application is considered. In others, you must leave on your original date unless the extension is granted. Never assume; check the official guidance and keep your application receipt with you.

What happens if your visa extension is refused?

If refused, you normally need to leave by the date stated in the decision. Staying after that is an overstay, which can lead to fines, detention, removal and bans. If you believe the decision is wrong, ask whether you can appeal or request a review, but follow the instructions about leaving.

How do you write a request letter for a visa extension?

Many immigration offices ask for a short letter explaining why you need more time. Keep it to one page and stick to the facts:

  1. Your details: full name, nationality, passport number and current visa or entry date.
  2. Your current end date and the new date you are asking for.
  3. The reason: for example "my flight was cancelled by the airline" or "I was admitted to hospital on 3 May".
  4. Evidence: list the documents you attach, such as a medical certificate or airline email.
  5. Funds and accommodation: explain how you will pay and where you will stay.
  6. Return plans: confirm your new booking home.
  7. Signature and date.

A clear letter makes the officer's job easier and shows that your request is genuine.

Visa extension or a new visa: which is better?

Sometimes a visa extension is not the best option. If your plans have changed completely, for example you now want to study or work, a new visa is usually the right route. Many countries do not allow you to switch from a visit visa to another type from inside the country. Compare the options:

Your situationUsually the better route
Flight cancelled or short delayExtension
Sudden illness or accidentExtension
Want a longer holiday where rules allowExtension, if permitted for tourists
Now want to study or workNew visa from your home country
Want to live with a partnerFamily visa through the proper route

What if you have a medical emergency?

A serious illness or accident is one of the most widely accepted reasons for a visa extension. Ask the hospital or doctor for a letter that states your condition in general terms, the treatment dates and when you are expected to be fit to travel. Contact your travel insurer early, because they may help with documents and costs. If you cannot visit the immigration office in person, ask whether a relative or representative can apply for you, or whether the application can be made online.

How much does it cost?

Fees vary widely by country and visa type, from modest local fees at an immigration office to higher charges for formal applications. Some extensions for force majeure may be free or reduced. Check the official fee list before you apply.

A real example: a cancelled flight in Spain

Leila, a teacher from Amman, visits Spain on a short Schengen visa. Two days before her flight home, the airline cancels all flights due to a strike, and the next available seat is after her visa ends. She visits the local immigration office with her passport, visa, the airline's cancellation email, her new booking and an updated insurance certificate. Her visa extension is approved for the extra days, and she leaves on her new flight without any problems.

Which visa extension mistakes should you avoid?

  • Applying after your stay has already ended
  • Assuming you can extend because a friend did in another country
  • Not extending travel insurance
  • Applying without evidence of your reason
  • Ignoring a refusal and staying longer
  • Working while on a visit visa, even during an extension

Key takeaways

  • A visa extension must be requested before your current permission ends.
  • Some countries allow easy extensions; others only in exceptional cases.
  • Schengen extensions are limited to force majeure, humanitarian or serious personal reasons.
  • Bring evidence, proof of funds, insurance and an onward ticket.
  • Never overstay while waiting unless the rules clearly allow it.

How can Alif Visa help with a visa extension?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping travellers worldwide. We can explain the rules for your country, help you prepare documents and arrange travel insurance for the extra days. Read our guide to visa refusal reasons, check your route, or talk to us.

Frequently asked questions

Can I extend a tourist visa?

It depends on the country. Some allow extensions easily, some only in exceptional cases, and some not at all.

When should I apply for a visa extension?

Before your current permission ends. Applying late can be treated as an overstay.

Can I extend a Schengen visa?

Only in limited situations, such as force majeure, serious illness or serious personal reasons.

Can I extend my stay in the UK as a visitor?

Usually only in limited cases. Most visitors leave and apply again for the right visa.

Can I extend an ESTA stay in the US?

Generally no. ESTA visitors normally cannot extend their stay.

Do I need new travel insurance?

Yes. Your insurance should cover the extra days.

What happens if I overstay while waiting?

It depends on the country's rules. In many places, an overstay can lead to fines or bans, so check the rules carefully.

Can someone else apply for a visa extension for me?

Some countries allow a representative to apply, for example if you are in hospital. Ask the immigration office what is accepted.

How long does a decision take?

It varies from the same day at some immigration offices to several weeks for formal applications, so apply as early as you can.

title: Where Can British Passport Holders Travel Without a Visa?
excerpt: Visa free countries for British passport holders: popular destinations, which need an ESTA, eTA or other online authorisation, passport validity rules and how to check before you go.
content:
Short answer: British passport holders can visit a large number of countries without a visa for short trips, including the Schengen Area, Turkey, Japan, Mexico, Brazil, South Africa and Morocco. Some "visa free countries" still ask for an online travel authorisation before you fly, such as an ESTA for the United States, an eTA for Canada, an eVisitor for Australia and an NZeTA for New Zealand. Rules change often, so check the official GOV.UK foreign travel advice for your destination before you book.

Quick factsDetails
Passport typeFull British citizen passport
Online authorisationsUSA (ESTA), Canada (eTA), Australia (eVisitor), New Zealand (NZeTA) and others
EuropeSchengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in 180
Passport validityMany countries require several months of validity
Best sourceGOV.UK foreign travel advice for each country

Table of Contents

  • What does "visa free" mean for British travellers?
  • Which popular visa free countries can British passport holders visit?
  • Which visa free countries need an online authorisation?
  • What about countries that are not visa free for British citizens?
  • How long can you stay in visa free countries?
  • What passport rules apply?
  • What do border officers ask in visa free countries?
  • How do the Entry/Exit System and ETIAS affect British travellers?
  • Do dual nationals or other UK passport types follow the same rules?
  • Are there visa free countries for UK residents who are not British citizens?
  • How can you plan a trip across several visa free countries?
  • Can you work or study in visa free countries?
  • Does a criminal record or previous refusal matter?
  • How do you check the rules before you travel?
  • A real example: a round-the-world trip
  • Should you still buy travel insurance for visa free trips?
  • Which mistakes should British travellers avoid?

  • How can Alif Visa help British travellers?
  • Frequently asked questions

What does "visa free" mean for British travellers?

A visa free trip means you do not need to apply for a visa at an embassy before you travel. You show your passport at the border and receive permission to enter, usually as a visitor for tourism, family visits or short business meetings. Visa free countries still set conditions: a maximum length of stay, a valid passport, and sometimes proof of a return ticket, accommodation or funds.

It does not mean you can work, study long-term or live there. For those, you normally need the right visa.

Which popular visa free countries can British passport holders visit?

DestinationWhat you need (short visits)
Schengen Area (e.g. France, Spain, Italy, Germany)No visa, up to 90 days in 180; Entry/Exit System applies
United StatesNo visa under the Visa Waiver Program, but an ESTA is required
CanadaNo visa if flying, but an eTA is required
AustraliaAn eVisitor or ETA is required before travel
New ZealandAn NZeTA is required before travel
JapanNo visa for short tourist visits
TurkeyNo visa for short tourist visits
MexicoNo visa for tourist visits
BrazilNo visa for tourist visits
South AfricaNo visa for short visits
MoroccoNo visa for short visits
ThailandVisa exemption for tourist visits; check the current length of stay
SingaporeNo visa for short visits; complete the arrival card online
United Arab EmiratesVisa on arrival for British citizens
South KoreaNo visa for short visits; check whether a K-ETA is needed

Lengths of stay and entry rules can change, so always confirm with GOV.UK before travelling.

Which visa free countries need an online authorisation?

Several visa free countries now use electronic travel authorisations. These are not visas, but you must get them before you fly.

  • United States – ESTA: apply online through the official US government website.
  • Canada – eTA: needed if you fly to or through Canada.
  • Australia – eVisitor or ETA: apply before travel; British citizens are usually eligible for an eVisitor.
  • New Zealand – NZeTA: apply before travel, with an International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy.
  • Schengen Area – ETIAS: planned for visa-exempt visitors after the Entry/Exit System; check the EU website for the start date.

Only use official government websites. Many unofficial sites charge extra fees for the same service.

What about countries that are not visa free for British citizens?

Some popular destinations do require a visa or e-visa for British passport holders, for example India and Vietnam for many types of visit, and Kenya requires an electronic travel authorisation. Rules for these countries can change, so check each one before you go. Alif Visa can help with the visa application where one is needed.

How long can you stay in visa free countries?

Each country sets its own limit. Common patterns are:

  • 90 days in any 180 days in the Schengen Area
  • 90 days in many other countries, such as Turkey and Japan for tourists
  • Up to six months in some countries, such as Canada, depending on the officer's decision
  • 30 days or less in some places

The officer at the border decides how long you can stay. Make sure you leave before the date you are given.

What passport rules apply?

Many visa free countries require your passport to be valid for a certain time beyond your stay:

  • Schengen Area: your passport must be less than 10 years old on the day you enter and valid for at least three months after the day you plan to leave.
  • Many other countries: at least six months' validity on arrival.
  • Blank pages: some countries require one or two blank pages for stamps.

Check your passport's issue and expiry dates well before you book.

What do border officers ask in visa free countries?

Even when you do not need a visa, border officers can ask questions before letting you in. Be ready to show:

  • a return or onward ticket
  • your accommodation address, such as a hotel booking or your host's details
  • enough money for your stay, for example a bank card or recent statement
  • travel insurance, which some countries strongly recommend or require
  • the purpose of your trip, explained in one sentence

Officers in visa free countries can still refuse entry if they are not satisfied, so keep these details easy to find on your phone or on paper.

How do the Entry/Exit System and ETIAS affect British travellers?

The EU's Entry/Exit System records British travellers' fingerprints, photos and entry and exit dates at Schengen borders. It replaced passport stamping and makes the 90/180 rule easier to enforce. On your first trip under the system, expect to register your biometrics at the border or at a kiosk, which can take extra time. ETIAS, a separate online travel authorisation for visa-exempt visitors, is planned next. Once it starts, British travellers will need to apply online before visiting most visa free countries in Europe.

Do dual nationals or other UK passport types follow the same rules?

Not always. The rules on this page are for full British citizen passports. Other British nationality passports, such as British National (Overseas), British Overseas Territories citizen or British Overseas citizen passports, can have different entry rules. Dual nationals should usually enter and leave a country using the same passport, and some countries require their own citizens to use their national passport. Check GOV.UK and the destination's official website for your passport type.

Are there visa free countries for UK residents who are not British citizens?

If you live in the UK but hold another passport, the list of visa free countries depends on your nationality, not your residence. However, a valid UK residence permit can sometimes help, for example when applying for visas to certain countries or for transit. Alif Visa helps UK residents of all nationalities check what they need.

How can you plan a trip across several visa free countries?

Multi-country trips need a little more planning. Write down each country, the dates you will be there and the entry rule for each one. Check transit rules for airports where you change planes, because some airports require a transit authorisation. Apply for all online authorisations at least a few weeks before you travel, and keep confirmation emails in one folder.

Can you work or study in visa free countries?

Usually no. Visa free entry is for visitors. You can often attend business meetings, conferences or short courses, but paid work, long courses and living there require a proper visa. Check each country's visitor rules.

Does a criminal record or previous refusal matter?

Some countries ask about past refusals, overstays or criminal records when you apply for an online authorisation or at the border. Answer honestly. If you have concerns, check the country's rules before you travel and get advice where needed.

How do you check the rules before you travel?

Follow these easy steps:

  1. Open the GOV.UK foreign travel advice page for your destination.
  2. Read the "Entry requirements" section carefully.
  3. Check passport validity and blank pages.
  4. Apply for any online authorisation on the official website.
  5. Check transit rules if you change planes in another country.
  6. Buy travel insurance before you go.
  7. Keep copies of your passport, authorisation and bookings.

A real example: a round-the-world trip

Sophie, a British nurse, plans a three-month trip to Japan, Australia, New Zealand and the United States. She checks GOV.UK for each country. Japan is visa free for her trip. For Australia she gets an eVisitor, for New Zealand an NZeTA, and for the United States an ESTA, all through official sites. She checks that her passport is valid for well over six months and buys travel insurance that covers all four countries. Her trip goes smoothly.

Should you still buy travel insurance for visa free trips?

Yes. Even when no visa or insurance certificate is required, medical treatment abroad can be very expensive, and the UK's Global Health Insurance Card only covers state healthcare in some European countries. Good travel insurance protects you against medical bills, cancellations and lost belongings wherever you go.

Which mistakes should British travellers avoid?

  • Forgetting an ESTA, eTA or other online authorisation
  • Using unofficial websites that charge extra
  • Travelling with a passport that is too old or close to expiry
  • Overstaying the permitted time
  • Assuming visa free means you can work
  • Relying on old information instead of current GOV.UK advice

Key takeaways

  • British passport holders can visit many visa free countries for short trips.
  • Some destinations still need an online authorisation, such as an ESTA or eTA.
  • Passport validity rules differ by country.
  • Visa free entry is for visits, not work or long stays.
  • Always check GOV.UK foreign travel advice before booking.

How can Alif Visa help British travellers?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company. We help British citizens and UK residents with visas and travel authorisations for countries that need them, and explain the rules for those that do not. Read our guide to the Schengen 90/180 rule, check your route, or talk to us.

Frequently asked questions

How many visa free countries can British citizens visit?

A large number, including the Schengen Area, Japan, Turkey, Mexico and many more. Check GOV.UK for the current list.

Do British citizens need a visa for the USA?

Not for short visits under the Visa Waiver Program, but an ESTA is required before travel.

Do British citizens need a visa for Europe?

Not for short visits to the Schengen Area, up to 90 days in any 180 days.

Do I need an eTA for Canada?

Yes, if you fly to or through Canada as a British citizen.

Is Australia visa free for British citizens?

You need an eVisitor or ETA, which you apply for online before travel.

Can I work in visa free countries?

Usually not. Visa free entry is for visits only.

Do I need a return ticket for visa free countries?

Many countries expect to see a return or onward ticket, and airlines may check this before you board.

Does my passport need to be valid for six months?

Many countries require this, while the Schengen Area requires at least three months after you leave and a passport less than 10 years old.

Will I need ETIAS for Europe?

ETIAS is planned for visa-exempt visitors, including British citizens. Check the official EU website for the start date before you travel.

Where can I check the latest rules?

The GOV.UK foreign travel advice pages list entry requirements for every country.

Sources

  • U.S. CBP: ESTA

title: How Do You Book a TLScontact Appointment?
excerpt: TLScontact appointment guide: how to book, reschedule and prepare for a TLScontact visa appointment for France, Belgium and other countries, plus fees and common mistakes.
content:
Short answer: A TLScontact appointment is a booked time at a TLScontact visa application centre, where you hand in your visa documents and give your fingerprints. TLScontact collects applications for several governments, including France and Belgium in many countries. To book a TLScontact appointment, create an account on the TLScontact website for your country and destination, fill in your application, choose a centre and time slot, and print your confirmation. The embassy or consulate makes the visa decision, not TLScontact.

Quick factsDetails
What TLScontact isA private company that runs visa application centres for embassies
Common destinationsFrance, Belgium and others, depending on the country you live in
Who decides your visaThe embassy or consulate
BookingOnline on the official TLScontact site for your country
What to bringAppointment confirmation, passport, form, photo and supporting documents

Table of Contents

  • How do you book a TLScontact appointment for Belgium in the UK?

What is a TLScontact appointment?

A TLScontact appointment is your time slot at a TLScontact visa application centre (VAC). At the appointment, staff check your documents, scan them, take your fingerprints and photo, collect the fees and send your file to the embassy. They also return your passport when the decision is made.

TLScontact is an outsourcing company. It does not decide visas and cannot influence the result. Its job is to make the collection of applications faster and more organised for the embassy.

Which countries use TLScontact?

TLScontact works for several governments, but which ones it serves depends on the country where you live. Common examples include:

  • France: in many countries, French visa applications go through TLScontact.
  • Belgium: in the UK, Belgian short-stay visa applications go through TLScontact centres in London, Edinburgh and Manchester.
  • Other countries: some embassies use TLScontact in certain countries and VFS Global or BLS International in others.

Always check the official website of the embassy you are applying to. It will tell you whether you need a TLScontact appointment, a VFS Global appointment, a BLS appointment or an embassy appointment.

How do you book a TLScontact appointment, step by step?

Booking a TLScontact appointment takes around 20 to 30 minutes if your documents are ready.

  1. Confirm TLScontact handles your application. Check the destination embassy's website for the country where you live.
  2. Open the official TLScontact website for your destination country and your country of residence.
  3. Create an account with your email address and a strong password, and confirm it from your inbox.
  4. Fill in your application. For France, you usually complete the France-Visas form first and then link it to TLScontact.
  5. Choose your centre based on where you live. Centres cover specific regions.
  6. Pick a date and time for your TLScontact appointment from the available slots.
  7. Print your confirmation and checklist, and keep them with your documents.

What should you bring to your TLScontact appointment?

Bring originals and a set of copies of everything on your checklist. For a short-stay Schengen visa, a typical file includes:

  • Appointment confirmation and the application form, signed
  • Passport valid for at least three months after your trip, with two blank pages, issued in the last ten years
  • Residence permit if you are not a citizen of the country where you apply
  • A recent passport photo that meets Schengen rules (see our visa photo guide)
  • Travel insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover for the whole Schengen area
  • Flight and hotel reservations, or an invitation from your host
  • Bank statements for the last three to six months and an employment or study letter
  • A short cover letter explaining your trip
  • Payment for the visa fee and the TLScontact service fee

How much does a TLScontact appointment cost?

Booking a standard TLScontact appointment is usually free. At the centre you pay:

  • the visa fee, which for Schengen visas is set by the EU (currently €90 for adults, less for children)
  • the TLScontact service fee, which varies by country
  • optional extras, such as SMS updates, courier return, photocopying, form-filling help or premium appointment slots

Premium slots, where offered, cost extra but give more flexible times. They do not make the embassy decide faster.

What happens at the TLScontact appointment?

On the day of your appointment:

  1. Arrive on time. Late arrivals may be turned away. Allow time for security checks.
  2. Check in with your confirmation and passport.
  3. Document check. Staff check your file against the checklist. They do not judge whether you will get the visa.
  4. Scanning. Your documents are scanned or sent to the embassy.
  5. Biometrics. Your fingerprints and photo are taken, unless you gave Schengen fingerprints in the last 59 months.
  6. Payment. You pay the fees and choose any optional services.
  7. Receipt. You receive a receipt with your reference number for tracking.

How do you reschedule or cancel a TLScontact appointment?

Log in to your TLScontact account and choose the option to change or cancel your appointment. Do this as early as possible, because slots fill up quickly. Rules on how often you can change and whether premium fees are refunded differ by country, so check the terms before you book a premium TLScontact appointment.

What if there are no TLScontact appointment slots?

  • Check early in the morning and at the start of the week, when new slots are often released.
  • Consider a premium slot if one is available and your trip is urgent.
  • Apply early: you can request a Schengen visa up to six months before travel.
  • Avoid websites or people selling appointments; they may be fake and can put your data at risk.

How do you track your application?

After your appointment, use the tracking tool in your TLScontact account or on the website with your reference number. Common stages are "application received", "sent to the consulate", "decision made" and "ready for collection" or "sent by courier". When your passport is ready, collect it or receive it by courier.

TLScontact appointment vs VFS Global vs BLS International

CompanyWhat it doesWho decides the visa
TLScontactRuns visa application centres for embassies such as France and Belgium in many countriesThe embassy or consulate
VFS GlobalRuns visa centres for many governments worldwideThe embassy or consulate
BLS InternationalRuns visa centres, best known for SpainThe embassy or consulate

You cannot choose between them. The embassy decides which company handles applications where you live. Read our BLS appointment guide if your destination uses BLS.

Which TLScontact appointment mistakes should you avoid?

  • Booking at a centre outside your area
  • Choosing the wrong visa type in the online form
  • Missing original documents or signatures
  • Bringing insurance that does not cover the whole Schengen area
  • Arriving late or without your confirmation
  • Paying unofficial agents for appointments

A real example: a TLScontact appointment for France

Leila, an Iranian citizen working as a software engineer in London, wants to visit Paris for a week. She completes the France-Visas form, which gives her a reference number, then opens the TLScontact website for France in the UK and books a appointment at the London centre. She brings her passport, UK residence permit, employer letter, payslips, bank statements, hotel booking, return train tickets and Schengen insurance. The appointment takes 30 minutes. She tracks her application online and collects her passport with a visa nine days later.

Tips for a smooth TLScontact appointment

  • Print the checklist for your exact visa type and use it to order your documents.
  • Bring copies of every page you hand in, in case staff ask for them.
  • Keep a pen and your reference numbers handy.
  • Wear clothing that does not cover your face or ears for the photo.
  • Bring the payment method the centre accepts.
  • For families, book a appointment for each traveller, or a group booking if the site allows it.

How do you book a TLScontact appointment for France?

France uses its own online system, France-Visas, together with TLScontact in many countries. The usual order is:

  1. Find the right visa type with the France-Visas "visa wizard".
  2. Create a France-Visas account and complete the online application.
  3. Print the application form and the receipt with your France-Visas reference.
  4. Follow the link to TLScontact, create your TLScontact account and book your appointment.
  5. Bring both the France-Visas printout and the TLScontact confirmation on the day.

If you skip France-Visas and only book with TLScontact, your file will be incomplete.

How do you book a TLScontact appointment for Belgium in the UK?

UK residents who need a Belgian short-stay visa apply through TLScontact centres in London, Edinburgh and Manchester. You create a TLScontact account, fill in the application, choose the centre for your area and book a appointment. Bring proof of UK residence and the documents on the TLScontact checklist. Our Belgium visa for UK residents guide explains the full process.

Can you get help at the centre?

Many centres offer paid help, such as form filling, photocopying, photos and document checks. These can be useful if you are short of time, but they are optional. They do not change the embassy's decision. Bringing a complete, well-organised file is the best way to make your appointment quick.

Is your data safe with TLScontact?

TLScontact handles applications under contract with the embassy and follows data protection rules. Protect yourself by booking only on the official website, using a strong password, and never sharing your account details with people offering to "help" with your appointment.

How early should you book your TLScontact appointment?

For Schengen visas you can apply up to six months before you travel and at least 15 days before. In busy seasons, such as summer and the weeks before Christmas, book your appointment as soon as your plans are fixed. Leave at least three to four weeks between the appointment and your trip for the decision and passport return.

Key takeaways

  • a appointment is where you hand in documents and give biometrics, not where your visa is decided.
  • Check the embassy website to confirm TLScontact handles your application.
  • Book online, choose the centre for your area, and print your confirmation.
  • Bring originals, copies, Schengen insurance and proof of residence.
  • Never buy appointments from unofficial sellers.

How can Alif Visa help with your TLScontact appointment?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping applicants worldwide. We check your documents, help you choose the right visa type, and prepare your file before your appointment. We also arrange travel insurance, flight reservations and hotel bookings. Read our Belgium visa guide, see our visa appointment service, or check your route.

Frequently asked questions

Is TLScontact the embassy?

No. TLScontact is a private company that collects visa applications for embassies. The embassy or consulate makes the decision.

Is booking a TLScontact appointment free?

A standard appointment is usually free to book. You pay the visa fee and TLScontact service fee at the centre.

Can I reschedule my TLScontact appointment?

Yes, usually through your TLScontact account, depending on slots and local rules.

Do premium TLScontact appointments speed up my visa?

No. Premium slots offer more convenient times, but the embassy's decision time stays the same.

Which countries use TLScontact?

It depends on where you live. France and Belgium use TLScontact in many countries. Check the embassy's website.

Do I need to give fingerprints at every TLScontact appointment?

Not always. If you gave Schengen fingerprints in the last 59 months, you may not need to give them again.

Can someone else attend my TLScontact appointment?

Usually no. You must attend in person to give biometrics, unless you are exempt.

title: What Is a Dummy Ticket for a Visa Application?
excerpt: Dummy ticket for visa explained: what a flight reservation is, when embassies accept it, how to get a genuine one with a PNR, and why fake tickets get visas refused.
content:
Short answer: A dummy ticket is a genuine flight reservation that you show with your visa application instead of a fully paid ticket. It has a real booking reference (PNR) that can be checked with the airline, but you have not bought the ticket yet. Many embassies, including Schengen embassies, say you should not buy tickets until your visa is approved, so a dummy ticket is normal and accepted. A fake or edited ticket is not a dummy ticket; it can get your visa refused and may count as fraud.

Quick factsDetails
What it isA real flight reservation or itinerary, not yet paid in full
Also calledFlight reservation, flight itinerary, onward ticket
Accepted byMost embassies for visit visas, including Schengen countries
Must haveYour name, flight details and a booking reference you can verify
Never useFake, edited or photoshopped tickets

What is a dummy ticket?

a reservation is a flight reservation made in your name for the dates you plan to travel, without paying for the full ticket. It shows the embassy your travel plan: when you will arrive, when you will leave and which airline you will use. Travel agents and airlines can create these reservations, and the booking normally exists for a limited time.

The word "dummy" is confusing. a reservation should be a real reservation that the embassy can check, not an invented document. Some people call it a "flight itinerary for visa" for that reason.

Why do embassies accept a dummy ticket?

Many embassies tell applicants not to buy non-refundable tickets before the visa is approved. If your visa is refused, you could lose the money. The European Commission's Schengen guidance, for example, asks for proof of travel plans rather than a paid ticket. a reservation solves this: it proves your plan without the financial risk.

When do you need a dummy ticket?

You may need a reservation when:

  • your visa checklist asks for a flight itinerary or reservation
  • you apply for a Schengen, UK, US, Canada or other visit visa and want to show return travel
  • you need proof of onward travel for a visa on arrival or an e-visa
  • an airline asks for proof of onward travel before letting you board on a one-way ticket

Always check your exact checklist. Some embassies accept an itinerary, while a few may later ask for a confirmed ticket before issuing the visa.

How do you get a genuine dummy ticket, step by step?

  1. Decide your travel dates. Match them to your visa application and hotel bookings.
  2. Choose a reliable source. A licensed travel agency, an airline's "hold" option, or a reputable reservation service.
  3. Give your details exactly as in your passport. Name spelling must match.
  4. Get a booking reference (PNR). This six-character code lets anyone check the reservation on the airline's website or through a travel agent.
  5. Check the reservation yourself on the airline's "manage booking" page if possible.
  6. Print it with your name, flight numbers, dates and booking reference clearly visible.
  7. Keep it valid until your appointment. Some reservations expire after a few days, so time it close to your appointment date.

How much does a dummy ticket cost?

Prices vary. Some airlines let you hold a fare for a small fee. Travel agencies may charge a service fee for a reservation. Many people pay a modest amount for a verifiable dummy ticket rather than risking a full fare. Alif Visa's flight reservation service provides reservations for visa applications.

Dummy ticket vs fake ticket: what is the difference?

Genuine dummy ticketFake ticket
Booking referenceReal, can be checkedInvented or copied
Created byAirline or travel agencyEdited by hand or software
Visa riskNormal, widely acceptedRefusal and possible ban
Legal riskNoneCan be treated as fraud

Embassies can and do check reservations. Submitting a fake document can lead to a refusal, a record on visa databases and, in some countries, a ban on future applications.

What should your dummy ticket show?

A good dummy ticket clearly shows:

  • your full name as in your passport
  • the airline, flight numbers and route
  • departure and arrival dates and times
  • a booking reference (PNR)
  • return or onward travel within your visa dates

If you travel to several countries, the reservation should show the full route, matching your itinerary and hotel bookings.

What if your dummy ticket expires before the decision?

That is normal. Embassies understand that reservations expire. What matters is that it was genuine when you submitted it. If the embassy asks for an updated itinerary, get a fresh reservation. Once your visa is approved, buy your real ticket for the dates on your visa.

Do you need a dummy ticket for every visa?

No. Some e-visas and visas on arrival do not ask for flight proof, and some embassies prefer a simple travel plan. Business travellers may be asked for an invitation letter instead of a strong itinerary. Always follow the checklist for your exact visa type.

A real example: a Schengen visit to Italy

Faisal, a Jordanian citizen living in Dubai, applies for an Italian Schengen visa to visit Rome for ten days. His checklist asks for a flight reservation. He asks a licensed travel agency for a reservation from Dubai to Rome and back, matching his hotel dates. The reservation has a booking reference he checks on the airline website. He submits it with his application. His visa is approved in eight days, and he then buys a real ticket for the same dates.

What are the most common dummy ticket mistakes?

  • Using a website that produces fake tickets with no real booking
  • Name spelling that does not match the passport
  • Dates that do not match the hotel bookings or visa application
  • A one-way reservation when the embassy needs proof of return
  • Reservations that expire weeks before the appointment
  • Buying a non-refundable ticket when a reservation would have been enough

How does a dummy ticket fit into your whole visa file?

a reservation is just one part of your file. Embassies look at everything together:

  • Purpose: your cover letter, invitation or tour plan
  • Money: your bank statements and income
  • Accommodation: hotel bookings or an invitation
  • Insurance: for Schengen visas, Schengen travel insurance with €30,000 cover
  • Return: your job, studies, family or property at home

When all of these tell the same story, your reservation supports a strong application.

What do different embassies say about flight bookings?

Requirements vary, so read your checklist:

  • Schengen countries: usually ask for proof of travel plans, such as a flight reservation, and advise against buying tickets before the visa is issued.
  • United Kingdom: visitor visa guidance does not require a booked ticket; a clear travel plan and dates are enough in most cases.
  • United States: the B1/B2 process does not require a ticket; your DS-160 asks for your intended dates.
  • Some e-visas and visas on arrival: may ask for proof of onward travel at the border or when boarding.

When an embassy does not ask for a reservation, you do not need to add one, but a clear travel plan always helps.

Airline "hold" options vs travel agency reservations

OptionHow it worksThings to check
Airline holdSome airlines let you hold a fare for a short time for a small feeHow long the hold lasts
Travel agency reservationAn agent creates a booking with a referenceThat the reference can be checked
Refundable ticketYou buy a fully refundable fare and cancel if refusedCancellation fees and refund time

All three can work. The key is that your reservation is genuine and matches your plans.

Can you change your dates after the visa is approved?

Yes, within reason. Your real ticket should fit inside the dates on your visa. If your visa allows 15 days from a certain date, travel within that window. Large changes, such as travelling months later, may need a new visa. Short changes within the validity are normal.

Dummy ticket for onward travel

Some countries and airlines ask for proof that you will leave, especially if you fly on a one-way ticket. A genuine onward dummy ticket can satisfy this check. Keep it on your phone and printed, and make sure it is still valid on the day you fly.

How do you spot a fake dummy ticket service?

Be careful with websites that promise an instant "ticket" for a very low price with no real airline booking behind it. Warning signs include:

  • no booking reference, or a reference that does not work on the airline's website
  • a document that looks like an e-ticket but has no ticket number or airline confirmation
  • promises that the document is "guaranteed accepted by all embassies"
  • no company name, address or customer support

A genuine dummy ticket service explains clearly that you are getting a reservation, gives you a reference you can check, and tells you how long it stays valid.

Hotel bookings work the same way

Embassies often ask for proof of accommodation alongside your reservation. Refundable hotel bookings or reservations with free cancellation serve the same purpose. Make sure the hotel dates match your flight dates exactly, and that the names match your passport.

Key takeaways

  • a reservation is a genuine flight reservation, not a paid ticket and not a fake.
  • Most embassies accept a reservation and advise against buying tickets before your visa.
  • Make sure it has a verifiable booking reference and your passport name.
  • Match the dates to your hotel bookings and visa application.
  • Never use fake or edited tickets.

Frequently asked questions

Is a dummy ticket legal?

Yes, if it is a genuine reservation made by an airline or travel agency. Fake or edited tickets are not legal and can lead to refusal or bans.

Do embassies check a dummy ticket?

They can. Embassies may check the booking reference with the airline, so it must be genuine.

How long is a dummy ticket valid?

It depends on the reservation. Many last from a few days to a few weeks. Time it close to your appointment.

Should I buy a real ticket before my visa?

Usually no. Most embassies advise waiting until your visa is approved.

Can I use a dummy ticket for a one-way trip?

For visit visas, embassies usually want to see return or onward travel, so include it.

Is a flight itinerary the same as a dummy ticket?

Yes, the terms are used for the same thing: a genuine reservation used for a visa application.

Can a dummy ticket get my visa refused?

A genuine one is normally fine. A fake one can lead to refusal and future problems.

What if my reservation expires before the embassy decides?

That is normally fine. Officers look at whether the booking was genuine when you applied. Once your visa is approved, buy your real ticket for the same dates if you can.

Do I need a hotel booking as well?

Most visit visas also ask for proof of accommodation, such as a refundable hotel booking or an invitation from your host. Make sure the dates match your flights.
